pages.title: Introduction
pages.text: $(thing)Paper$() is either made from the processed stalk of the $(l:the_world/wild_crops#papyrus)Papyrus$() crop, from $(l:agriculture/papermaking#parchment)Animal Hides$(), or from a lengthy process using specific types of $(l:agriculture/papermaking#paper_from_wood)Wood$(). Paper is useful for many things―like $(item)Backpacks$() and $(item)Nametags$()―but most importantly it is required for progression into the $(thing)Electric Age$()!

pages.title: Paper from Papyrus
pages.text: Paper can be directly sourced from the $(l:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papyrus)Papyrus$() crop. Papyrus must first be cut into strips with a $(thing)Knife$()...

pages.title: Soaked Papyrus Strip
pages.text: Then, papyrus strips are soaked in a $(l:craftsmanship/barrels)Barrel$() of $(thing)Water$().

pages.title: Unrefined Paper
pages.text: Then, soaked papyrus strips are woven together in a $(l:agriculture/weaving#loom)Loom$() to make $(thing)Unrefined Paper$(). Finally, it must be placed on a log and $(l:agriculture/leather_making#scraping)Scraped$() to make $(thing)Paper$().

$(thing)Parchment Paper$() starts with a $(l:agriculture/leather_making#scraping)Scraped Hide$(). Parchment requires treatment with a few different items. First, $(thing)Pumice$() is needed. Pumice is found on the ground near $(l:the_world/geology)Volcanoes$(), rarely from $(l:craftsmanship/panning)Panning$(), or from raiding the chests of locals.
pages.title: Parchment
Treated Hide
pages.text: Crafting pumice, a hammer, and scraped hide gives sections of $(thing)Treated Hide$().

pages.title: Parchment Paper
pages.text: Treated hide, $(l:craftsmanship/glassworking#lime_and_potash)lime powder$(), flour, and a fresh egg will complete the treatment process and yield usable paper.

$(thing)Creating Paper from Wood$() is an ancient process that requires processing of sturdy types of wood into sheets, which are broken down into a pulp, and then pressed, dried and scraped to make paper.$(br2)Note that softer types of wood are not suitable for making paper, only $(t:#tfg:hardwood)$(6)Hardwoods$() can produce paper.
pages.title: Paper from Wood
Stripped Hardwood
pages.text: The process begins by stripping the $(t:#tfg:hardwood)$(6)Hardwood's$() bark off to expose the internal fibers of the log, You can strip the log by placing it down and $(item)$(k:key.use)$() it with an axe.

pages.title: Hardwood Strip
pages.text: Next, the stripped wood is shaven with an axe to obtain $(item)Hardwood Strips$(). This can be done using an Axe or more sophisticated methods later.

pages.title: Soaked Hardwood Strip
pages.text: Then, the individual strips are soaked in a $(l:craftsmanship/barrels)Barrel$() of $(thing)Water$(). This $(thing)debilitates the structural integrity$() of the $(thing)wood$() so it can be $(thing)broken down further$().

pages.title: Hardwood Pulp
pages.text: Afterward, utilize the $(l:craftsmanship/quern)Quern$() to break down the soaked strips into $(item)Hardwood Pulp$().

pages.title: Piling up the Pulp
pages.text: While the quern gives you small piles of pulp, you'll want to combine them together in a $(thing)Workbench$(). More advanced methods of crushing the strips yield higher amounts of pulp.

pages.title: Breaking down the Pulp
pages.text: Before the pulp can be processed further into paper, it needs to be broken down further by $(thing)Boiling it with Lye$() in a $(l:cooking/cooking_methods#vat)Vat$() or a $(l:cooking/cooking_methods#pot)Pot$().

pages.title: Pressing the Pulp
pages.text: After broken down by boiling it with Lye, the $(item)Thermochemically Treated Hardwood Pulp$() can be pressed down into a sheet of $(item)Soaked Unrefined Paper$(). You can stomp the treated hardwood pulp in a $(l:cooking/alcohol#grape_smashing)Stomping Barrel$() into sheets, or you can use an $(l:craftsmanship/anvils)Anvil$().
The final step is $(l:cooking/decay#drying)Drying$() the $(item)Soaked Unrefined Paper$() into $(item)Unrefined Paper$(), Which then can be Scraped into $(item)Paper$() as shown before.

pages.title: Cutting Steps...?
pages.text: Advancing in the Tech-Tree will allow you to create paper from wood with less overall steps, check $(d)E$(a)M$(b)I$() for the different approaches you can take for making paper with wood.
